catalog.title: Tool catalog — {{name}}

add.title: Add application
add.description: Choose an existing application or create one as part of the same connection flow. Credentials stay as vault references and the connection is probed before activation.
add.appTypeInferred: Application type is inferred from the transport you choose next.
add.templateNote: Only board-approved command templates can run. Arbitrary commands are never accepted.
add.vaultNote: Free-text secrets are not accepted — pick a vault entry; Paperclip stores only the vault:// reference and resolves it at gateway use time.
add.probeNote: Probe latency is a single round-trip sample. Aggregate p95 latency across traffic is tracked on the Runtime tab once the connection is live.

pasteConfig.headerSubtitle: Paste the MCP config snippet from the tool's README and we'll turn it into a friendly setup.
pasteConfig.invalidJson: That doesn't look like valid JSON yet — paste the whole snippet, including the outer braces.
pasteConfig.helperText: Paste an MCP config — the snippet a README tells you to copy.
pasteConfig.showBeforeSave: We'll read it and show what we found before anything is saved.
pasteConfig.emptyDraft: We couldn't find an app in that config. Double-check you pasted the whole snippet.
pasteConfig.remoteNote: Checking a remote app creates a draft connection, stores any header replacements as Paperclip secrets, and runs health/catalog discovery before activation.
pasteConfig.stdioNote: We humanized the field names from the config. These run-in-your-workspace tools stay as drafts until an admin maps them to an approved template.
pasteConfig.keysStayDraft: Keys from this config stay draft-only until an admin maps them to an approved template.
pasteConfig.reviewSubtitle: Health and catalog checks passed. Every discovered action starts allowed; you can narrow access after activation.
